A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.
Next I'll compare per-service span counts, error rates and mean latency between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)*1.0/count(*) err FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)*1.0/count(*) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The `ts-seat-service` slowdown sits in its own `SeatController.getLeftTicketOfInterval` method, with its `GET` client calls also slow. I'll check which downstream services those calls reach and how the spans are parented.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name psvc, p.span_name pname, c.service_name csvc, c.span_name cname, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) c_ms, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) p_ms FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id = p.trace_id WHERE p.attr_span_kind='Client' AND p.service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-route-service','ts-travel2-service','ts-travel-service') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: Seat-service's `GET` calls to config-service take only ~3 ms in the child span, yet the parent takes ~43 ms, so the time is being spent inside seat-service itself. Next I'll check resource metrics for seat-service and travel-plan-service.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-route-service') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Resource metrics for seat, travel-plan and route are flat, so this doesn't look like container saturation. I'll check logs next, then look at one slow seat trace end-to-end.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE level<>'INFO' OR service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-travel-plan-service') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC

WITH s AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-seat-service' AND span_name LIKE 'POST /api/v1/seatservice%' AND duration > 500000000 LIMIT 1) SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, span_id, parent_span_id, round(duration/1e6,1) ms, time FROM abnormal_traces WHERE trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM s) ORDER BY time

content.text: The seat-service slowdown is inside its own method, and travel-plan and travel2 inherit it. Route-service's DB client spans went from ~41k to ~97k, which is out of proportion to its request count, so I'll compare its operations between periods.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT 'n' p, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) c, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) ms FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-route-service' GROUP BY 2,3), b AS (SELECT 'a' p, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) c, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-route-service' GROUP BY 2,3) SELECT coalesce(a.span_name,b.span_name) s, coalesce(a.k,b.k) k, a.c nc, b.c ac, a.ms nms, b.ms ams FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.span_name=b.span_name AND a.k=b.k ORDER BY ac DESC NULLS LAST

content.text: Route-service's per-operation timings are nearly unchanged; the extra DB spans mostly reflect more traffic, so it isn't a root cause. Next I'll check restarts/uptime and network metrics for the whole system to rule out other faults.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric ILIKE '%restart%' OR metric ILIKE '%uptime%' OR metric ILIKE '%retrans%' OR metric ILIKE '%drop%' OR metric ILIKE '%hubble%' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 60

SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric ILIKE '%restart%' OR metric ILIKE '%uptime%' OR metric ILIKE '%jvm%' OR metric ILIKE '%gc%' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 60
